candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — pain management and nonpharmacological comfort interventions
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — pain assessment and evaluation
candidate.educational_objective: Reassess pain, function, and treatment effects after an analgesic at an interval appropriate to the intervention rather than relying on a fixed universal time or physiologic signs alone.

options.A: Document the medication as given and wait until the next shift to assess the client's response
options.B: Reassess pain and function at a time appropriate to the medication's route and expected onset or peak, and evaluate for adverse effects
options.C: Reassess only if the client requests another dose because the original pain score already established the need for treatment
options.D: Use changes in heart rate and blood pressure instead of asking the client about pain because physiologic signs are more reliable than self-report

candidate.rationale: Evaluation is part of the nursing process. After a pain intervention, the nurse reassesses whether the intervention achieved the client's comfort and functional goals and whether adverse effects occurred. The timing should reflect the route and expected onset/peak rather than an arbitrary universal interval. Self-report remains central when the client can communicate.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Pain interventions require reassessment for effectiveness, with timing individualized to the medication route/onset/peak rather than one universal interval.
candidate.source_locator: Comfort — Evaluation: regularly evaluate intervention effectiveness; after analgesics reassess in about an hour or another time frame based on route, onset, and peak; follow up if ineffective
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
candidate.stem: A postoperative client reports pain of 8/10 and receives an analgesic. Which action best demonstrates appropriate nursing evaluation of the intervention?
